rubric.evidence: Every signature and constraint traced to the webrtc-extensions Editor's Draft fetched live 2026-10-25: verbatim partial-interface + dictionary IDL, the [[RTCDiagnosticLoggingSessionId]] internal slot, each method's algorithm steps (TypeError on >5 metadata entries or >100-char key/value; InvalidStateError on double-start or stop/cancel without a session; RFC 4122 §4.4 UUID recommendation with the spec's own anti-fingerprinting rationale; stop keeps data, cancel MUST remove it), plus the section's dedicated Security and Privacy text. Shipping state from the runtime flag record (default stable, Android not enabled), the ChromeStatus API record (desktop 156, android null), both resolved blink-dev intent threads, the tracking bug, and the enterprise policy named in the record's own summary.

Feature id 5091582546149376 confirmed in the milestone=156 listing under 'Enabled by default' (fetched 2026-10-25); slug webrtc-diagnostic-logging-api derived from the exact listing name 'WebRTC Diagnostic Logging API' per invariant #1; H1 uses the listing name. The desktop-only reality (no Android milestone; flag record Android:"") is disclosed in the banner, context, and compat table rather than smoothed over.

The whole developer-facing surface is three static methods, one single-member dictionary, and the session-slot lifecycle; all six items are inventoried with nine-dimension mappings. Each method gets its own full reference subsection (parameters, return, errors, behavior) rather than a compressed two-column table; the stop-vs-cancel data-retention difference and the one-session-per-global rule get a dedicated state-transition table.

The page leads with the API's defining inversion — logs never reach the page, success is unobservable — and keeps restating what that means at each decision point (no feedback to display in the example; a demo could only show the UUID). The static-not-instance nature and per-global (not per-connection) scope are called out explicitly.

A support-flow example exercising all three methods, the metadata limits, both throwable errors, and feature detection; labelled gendn-derived from the method contracts. Not executed in a Chrome 156 desktop build in this environment (verification Chromium predates the API); behavior is documented from the spec algorithms.
